title: Bounded-Residue No-Carry Zero-Detection Theorem
statement: Let r=(r_0,...,r_{m-1}) be an integer vector with |r_j|<=A. For Phi_B(r)=sum_j r_j B^j and m>=2, Phi_B(r)=0 implies r=0 for every such r iff B>A.
proof_core: At the least nonzero coordinate t, B divides r_t. If 0<|r_t|<B this is impossible. Sharpness for B<=A is witnessed by (-B,1,0,...).
novelty_boundary: Elementary/classical arithmetic; rediscovered and sharpened inside the campaign. Historical novelty not claimed.

title: Sharp Balanced-Cube Injectivity Theorem
statement: Phi_B is injective on [-A,A]^m ∩ Z^m iff B>2A (for m>=2). The least integer base is 2A+1.
proof_core: Equality Phi_B(x)=Phi_B(y) reduces to zero detection for x-y in [-2A,2A]^m. If B<=2A, choose two cube points whose difference is (-B,1,0,...).
novelty_boundary: Classical balanced positional representation fact; exact sharp statement is an important campaign asset.

title: Carry-Lattice Kernel Generation Theorem
statement: The integer kernel of Phi_B: Z^m -> Z is generated by the adjacent carry vectors g_j = B e_j - e_{j+1}, j=0,...,m-2.
proof_core: Eliminate coordinates iteratively: kernel membership forces the current least coordinate to be divisible by B, allowing subtraction of an integer multiple of g_j.
novelty_boundary: Standard module/kernel calculation; useful because it completely characterizes every positional collision.

title: Sharp Relation-Localization Theorem
statement: For coefficients a=(a_1,...,a_n), digit alphabet D, and M=max{|sum_l a_l d_l|: d_l∈D}, every global relation sum_l a_l x_l=0 in the digit language localizes coordinatewise whenever B>M.
proof_core: The global relation is Phi_B of the coordinate-residue vector, whose digits have magnitude at most M.
novelty_boundary: Classical no-carry lifting mechanism; important reusable theorem schema.

title: Integer-Root Divisibility Threshold
statement: For every nonzero integer polynomial whose nonzero coefficients have absolute value at most C, positive integer evaluation at B is guaranteed nonzero for the entire class iff B>C.
proof_core: Factor out the least power of X. If B is a root, B divides the resulting nonzero constant term. Sharpness for B<=C is P(X)=X-B.
novelty_boundary: An elementary consequence of the rational/integer root principle; not historically novel. Its value is the exact closure and the elimination of term-count-dependent estimates.

title: Positional Sparsity-Impossibility Corollary
statement: Sparsity, degree, or term count cannot lower the universal positional base below 2A+1 for signed coordinate alphabet [-A,A], because the sharp obstruction already has support two.
proof_core: The collision polynomial X-B, equivalently the adjacent carry vector (-B,1), is already 2-sparse.
novelty_boundary: Logical corollary of CF-05; a permanent governor against a large dead search family.

title: Output-Span Lower Bound for Linear Scalarization
statement: If x -> w·x is injective on [-A,A]^m, then ||w||_1 >= ((2A+1)^m-1)/(2A).
proof_core: The cube has (2A+1)^m points, while every output lies in an interval containing 2A||w||_1+1 integers.
novelty_boundary: Elementary counting bound.

title: Optimality of Balanced Positional Weights
statement: Balanced positional weights (1,q,...,q^{m-1}) with q=2A+1 attain the minimum possible output span and coefficient l1 norm among integer linear scalarizations injective on the full cube.
proof_core: The geometric-series norm meets BOX-01 exactly; injectivity follows from CF-02.
novelty_boundary: Classical mixed-radix optimality in a precise extremal formulation; historical novelty not claimed.

title: Rigidity of the Full-Box Optimizer
statement: Equality in the full-box output-span bound forces positional weights, up to coordinate permutation and independent sign changes.
proof_core: After shifting balanced digits to {0,...,q-1}, equality makes the image a bijection onto every integer 0,...,q^m-1. Gap-or-collision induction forces weights 1,q,q^2,...
novelty_boundary: Plausibly classical canonical-numeration rigidity; proof should be formalized and literature-checked.

title: Mixed-Radix Extremality for Heterogeneous Boxes
statement: For a rectangular product of digit alphabets of sizes q_0,...,q_{m-1}, mixed-radix weights 1,q_0,q_0q_1,... attain the minimum contiguous output span. The clean uniqueness claim requires an ordering convention compatible with the coordinate capacities.
proof_core: Counting gives span at least product(q_i)-1; mixed radix is bijective onto the full interval.
novelty_boundary: Classical mixed-radix numeration. The exact rigidity statement deserves careful formal wording.

title: No Unbounded Additive Embedding Z^m -> Z
statement: For m>1, no additive group homomorphism Z^m -> Z is injective. Exact one-scalar additivity is possible only after restricting the domain, bounding it, or weakening recovery.
proof_core: Every homomorphism is x -> w·x and has a rank-(at least m-1) kernel.
novelty_boundary: Basic abelian-group rank fact; crucial constitutional limit.

title: Net-Balance Insufficiency for Prefix-Constrained Languages
statement: No checker depending only on terminal additive totals can characterize a language whose validity depends on prefix order. (+1,-1) and (-1,+1) have equal totals but different prefix validity.
proof_core: Explicit two-word counterexample.
novelty_boundary: Elementary automata/monoid observation; high-value architecture governor.

title: Sparse Moment Uniqueness Theorem
statement: An integer vector with support at most 2s is determined by its first 2s power moments sum_i z_i i^r, r=0,...,2s-1.
proof_core: Restrict to the nonzero support and invert the resulting Vandermonde matrix.
novelty_boundary: Classical Prony/Vandermonde uniqueness principle; useful exact reduction.

title: Sparse Carry-Free Moment Encoding
statement: The weights w_i=sum_{r=0}^{2s-1} i^r B^r with B>4As m^{2s-1} yield an injective integer-linear scalar encoding of all s-sparse vectors in [-A,A]^m.
proof_core: No-carry extraction recovers all 2s moments of the difference; SP-01 forces equality.
novelty_boundary: Likely a rediscovery/combination of sparse interpolation and positional packing. Historical novelty unverified.

title: Finite-Field Sparse Syndrome Injectivity
statement: For p>max(m,2A) and distinct alpha_i∈F_p, the first 2s Vandermonde syndromes sum_i x_i alpha_i^r uniquely determine every s-sparse integer vector x∈[-A,A]^m.
proof_core: A collision gives a 2s-sparse field vector in a square Vandermonde nullspace; coefficient lifting is unique because p>2A.
novelty_boundary: Classical Reed–Solomon syndrome / sparse interpolation mathematics.

title: Two-s Measurements Lower Bound — Corrected Scope
statement: At least 2s linear field measurements are necessary to recover every s-sparse vector over the whole field. This lower bound does not automatically prove 2s optimality for a restricted bounded integer alphabet embedded in the field.
proof_core: Any r×m matrix has a dependent set of at most r+1 columns. For r<2s this yields a nonzero kernel vector of support≤2s over the field.
novelty_boundary: Standard spark bound. The corrected scope must be retained in every future claim.

title: Robust Packed Sparse-Syndrome Correction
statement: Adding an [2s+2t,2s,2t+1] MDS outer code corrects t arbitrary corrupted syndrome channels before sparse-state recovery, while preserving linear aggregation and carry-free packing.
proof_core: MDS decoding recovers the syndrome message; SP-03 then recovers the sparse state.
novelty_boundary: Classical coding-theoretic composition; valuable exact architecture theorem.

title: Optimal Linear Channel Redundancy
statement: A 2s-symbol linear syndrome message needs at least 2t extra field symbols to correct t arbitrary channel errors, and at least t extra symbols to detect t errors or correct t known erasures. MDS codes attain these bounds.
proof_core: Minimum-distance requirements plus the Singleton bound.
novelty_boundary: Classical coding theory.

title: Binary Sparse Additive Encoding Lower Bound
statement: If positive weights up to W uniquely encode every subset of [m] of size at most s by its sum, then sW+1 >= sum_{r=0}^s binom(m,r), hence W=Omega_s(m^s).
proof_core: Count legal subsets and possible sums in [0,sW].
novelty_boundary: Elementary counting bound in B_s/Sidon territory.

title: Shifted B_s Encoding for Variable-Cardinality Subsets
statement: Given a cyclic B_s set a_i mod N, weights w_i=L+a_i with L=s(N-1)+1 uniquely encode every subset of size at most s by its integer sum.
proof_core: The large shift first forces equal cardinalities; reduction mod N plus equal padding to s terms invokes the B_s property.
novelty_boundary: B_s construction is classical; the exact variable-cardinality shift and system use should be literature-checked.

title: Optimal Binary Sparse Exponent
statement: For fixed s, the minimum possible largest positive weight for exact additive encoding of all subsets of [m] of size at most s satisfies W(m,s)=Theta_s(m^s).
proof_core: Combine BS-01 with a prime-power cyclic B_s construction and BS-02.
novelty_boundary: Closely connected to classical B_s sequence theory; not claimed as historically new.

title: Signed Two-Sparse Counting Lower Bound
statement: Any positive-weight scalar encoding of every x∈{-1,0,1}^m with support at most two requires max_i w_i >= m^2/2.
proof_core: There are 2m^2+1 legal states and only 4W+1 possible sums in [-2W,2W].
novelty_boundary: Elementary counting lower bound.

title: Shifted Sidon Encoding for Signed Two-Sparse States
statement: If {a_i} is a Sidon set in [0,N] and L>4N, then weights w_i=L+a_i uniquely encode all {-1,0,1}-valued states of support at most two.
proof_core: The shift separates total signed charge in {-2,-1,0,1,2}. Sidon sums resolve equal-sign pairs; Sidon differences resolve opposite-sign ordered pairs.
novelty_boundary: Sidon theory is classical; this precise signed-charge construction and application require novelty review.

title: Optimal Signed Two-Sparse Exponent
statement: For positive weights exactly encoding every {-1,0,1}-valued support-two state, the optimal largest-weight growth is Theta(m^2).
proof_core: Combine SGN-01 with SGN-02 and classical O(m^2)-range Sidon sets.
novelty_boundary: Likely a direct corollary of generalized Sidon/linear-form theory; historical novelty unverified.

title: Bounded Signed Sparse Exponent Conjecture
statement: For every fixed coefficient bound A and sparsity s, the minimum largest positive integer weight required to encode every s-sparse vector in [-A,A]^m exactly satisfies W_A(m,s)=Theta_{A,s}(m^s).
evidence: The binary case A=1 with coefficients {0,1} has Theta_s(m^s).
The first genuinely signed case {-1,0,1}, s=2 has Theta(m^2).
Signs did not double the exponent in the first nontrivial case.
risk: Unknown for s>=3/general A in this estate. A counterexample may force a larger exponent. Generic B_h and union-bound constructions are too expensive and do not settle the exponent.
novelty_boundary: This is the central live theorem target. It must be literature-checked before any novelty claim.

title: Signed Three-Sparse Theta(m^3) Conjecture
statement: For x∈{-1,0,1}^m with support at most three, the optimal largest positive weight is Theta(m^3).
evidence: The charge-separation method closes s=2 but new three-way signed linear-form collisions appear at s=3.
A coefficient-profile separator plus a finite family of linear-form Sidon cores may plausibly give O(m^3).
risk: No construction or impossibility proof has yet been produced in the campaign.
novelty_boundary: Potentially publication-relevant if not already contained in linear-form Sidon literature.

title: Layered Coefficient-Profile Separator Heuristic
statement: A near-optimal signed sparse construction may separate coarse coefficient statistics using widely spaced layers, then use coefficient-aware linear-form Sidon cores to identify the coordinate assignment without paying an As exponent.
risk: The layering can silently inflate weight growth; no proof yet controls all cross-profile collisions.
novelty_boundary: Search program, not a theorem.
